provenance.title: Cardiovascular disease — total-risk management, the blood-pressure treatment threshold, and the statin indication
provenance.primarySource: WHO HEARTS technical package for cardiovascular disease management; WHO package of essential noncommunicable disease interventions (WHO PEN)
provenance.why: The change WHO HEARTS makes is to treat cardiovascular risk as a total, not a single number. A person is managed on their combined 10-year risk of a heart attack or stroke, not on blood pressure or cholesterol read in isolation — because the same systolic pressure carries very different absolute risk in a 40-year-old non-smoker and a 60-year-old smoker with diabetes. So the rules here work off a total-risk score where the caller supplies one, and off the individual thresholds (blood pressure, established disease, diabetes) that HEARTS still treats as standalone triggers when they cross a line. The statin decision is deliberately gated on total risk, established disease, or diabetes-with-age rather than on a blood pressure or an arithmetic age derivation, because that is how HEARTS frames who benefits.

sourceVerification.note: The WHO HEARTS / WHO PEN DAK is NOT vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. Authored against the published HEARTS technical package and WHO PEN protocols; ships ENGINEERING_SEED until the primary text is vendored. The structure is WHO-invariant: manage on total cardiovascular risk, treat a sustained systolic at or above 140 mmHg, apply a tighter target in diabetes, offer a statin to established disease / high total risk / diabetes with age, and review a systolic at or above 180 mmHg the same day. The exact national numbers — the risk band that defines 'high', the diabetes blood-pressure target, and the statin age cut-off — are MoHCC's to ratify; the values encoded here are the WHO reference thresholds used as placeholders.

rules.name: High total cardiovascular risk — intensive management
rules.message: High total cardiovascular risk (10-year risk 20% or more) — manage intensively.
rules.explanation: WHO HEARTS manages people on their total 10-year cardiovascular risk rather than a single measurement. A 10-year risk of 20% or more marks the high-risk group who gain the most from combined intervention — blood-pressure lowering, a statin, and aspirin where indicated — alongside lifestyle measures, regardless of whether any single reading looks alarming on its own.
rules.requiredAction: Enrol in intensive cardiovascular risk management: lifestyle counselling, blood-pressure lowering to target, a statin, and aspirin where indicated, with scheduled follow-up.
sourceRefs: WHO HEARTS technical package — total cardiovascular risk management; WHO PEN risk-based protocol

adaptation.whoStatement: People with a total 10-year cardiovascular risk of 20% or higher should receive intensive combined risk management.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published; the risk band that defines 'high' is a national ratification decision.

testCases.name: 10-year risk of 10% is not high risk here
no risk score supplied never reads as high risk

rules.name: Sustained systolic 140 mmHg or more — start antihypertensive treatment
rules.message: Sustained systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg or more — start antihypertensive treatment.
rules.explanation: WHO HEARTS treats a sustained systolic pressure at or above 140 mmHg as the threshold to begin drug treatment alongside lifestyle measures. The word that matters is sustained — the decision rests on repeated readings, not a single elevated measurement, which the caller confirms before this fires.
rules.requiredAction: Confirm the elevation on repeat readings, then start antihypertensive treatment per protocol and enrol in blood-pressure follow-up.
sourceRefs: WHO HEARTS technical package — hypertension treatment protocol; WHO PEN

adaptation.whoStatement: Antihypertensive treatment should be started at a sustained systolic pressure of 140 mmHg or higher.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published; confirmation on repeat readings is assumed before the threshold is acted on.

testCases.name: systolic 130 is below the treatment threshold
no blood pressure supplied never reads as at-threshold

rules.name: Diabetes with systolic 130 mmHg or more — tighter blood-pressure target
rules.message: Person with diabetes and systolic 130 mmHg or more — treat to the tighter diabetes target.
rules.explanation: Diabetes multiplies cardiovascular risk at any given blood pressure, so WHO HEARTS applies a lower treatment target in people with diabetes than in the general hypertensive population. A systolic at or above 130 mmHg in someone with diabetes warrants intensifying treatment toward that tighter target rather than the standard one.
rules.requiredAction: Intensify antihypertensive treatment toward the tighter diabetes target and review glycaemic control; schedule closer follow-up.
sourceRefs: WHO HEARTS technical package — blood-pressure targets in diabetes; WHO PEN diabetes protocol

adaptation.rationale: Encodes a lower systolic action threshold (130 mmHg) for people with diabetes than the general 140 mmHg threshold, reflecting HEARTS' tighter diabetes target. The exact diabetes target is a national ratification decision; 130 mmHg is used as the WHO reference placeholder.
adaptation.whoStatement: People with diabetes should be treated to a lower blood-pressure target than the general hypertensive population.
adaptation.nationalStatement: A tighter systolic action threshold of 130 mmHg is applied in diabetes pending national ratification of the exact target.

testCases.name: diabetes with systolic 135 crosses the tighter target
diabetes with systolic 125 is within the tighter target
no diabetes — the tighter target does not apply
diabetes but no blood pressure supplied never reads as at-threshold

rules.name: Statin indicated — established CVD, high total risk, or diabetes with age
rules.message: Statin indicated — established cardiovascular disease, high total risk, or diabetes with age.
rules.explanation: WHO HEARTS offers a statin to three groups: anyone with established cardiovascular disease (secondary prevention), anyone at high total 10-year risk, and people with diabetes above a defined age. The indication is framed on established disease, total risk, and diabetes-with-age rather than on a cholesterol reading, because those are the groups in whom benefit is established. Age is read here as ageMonths, where 480 months is 40 years.
rules.requiredAction: Offer a statin at the protocol dose alongside lifestyle measures, and enrol in cardiovascular follow-up to monitor adherence and tolerance.
sourceRefs: WHO HEARTS technical package — statin therapy for cardiovascular risk; WHO PEN

adaptation.whoStatement: A statin should be offered to people with established cardiovascular disease, those at high total cardiovascular risk, and people with diabetes above a defined age.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published; the statin age cut-off in diabetes (encoded as 40 years) is a national ratification decision.

testCases.name: high total risk indicates a statin
no established disease, low risk, no diabetes — not indicated
diabetes but under 40 with low risk — not indicated on these grounds
no inputs supplied never reads as a statin indication

rules.name: Systolic 180 mmHg or more — same-day review
rules.message: Systolic blood pressure of 180 mmHg or more — review the same day.
rules.explanation: A systolic pressure at or above 180 mmHg is severe hypertension. WHO HEARTS treats this as needing same-day clinical assessment for symptoms and signs of target-organ damage — chest pain, breathlessness, neurological signs, visual change — rather than a routine review appointment, because a hypertensive emergency at this level needs immediate action.
rules.requiredAction: Assess the same day for symptoms and signs of a hypertensive emergency (target-organ damage); if present, treat or refer urgently, otherwise start or intensify treatment with early follow-up.
sourceRefs: WHO HEARTS technical package — severe hypertension and hypertensive emergency; WHO PEN

adaptation.whoStatement: A systolic pressure of 180 mmHg or higher requires same-day clinical assessment for a hypertensive emergency.

testCases.name: systolic 160 is not severe enough for this rule
no blood pressure supplied never triggers a same-day review
